text.p: A Gary McAllister penalty in the 50th minute gave Scotland a 1-0 World Cup qualifying win over Belarus on Sunday but goalkeeper Jim Leighton was the hero for his injury-hit side.
The European group four win took the Scots seven points clear of second-placed Austria who were playing Latvia later on Sunday. Sweden, one point behind the Austrians, were away to Estonia.
The breakthrough arrived after Hibernian striker Darren Jackson was clumsily fouled in the box, giving the Scotland captain the chance to decide the match.
"I was absolutely sure I'd score," the Coventry midfielder said afterwards, adding that Andrei Satsunkevich in the Belarus goal had moved too soon.

Belarus, anchored at the bottom of the group, fought well in the first half with Scotland facing a strong wind. They forced Leighton into some fine saves, including two free kicks turned on to the post.
Scotland recovered but apart from occasional forays by Jackson, rarely threatened.
Belarus might count themselves unfortunate not to have forced an equaliser in a final 10 minutes of pressure during which Leighton was again at the fore.

"I'm very pleased to come away with a win. The players were very tired at the end of the season," said Scotland coach Craig Brown, singling out his goalkeeper and the rest of the defence for praise and forecasting a bright future for Belarus soccer.
"I don't think Sweden and Austria will come here and take six points," he said. Both sides have yet to make the trip to Minsk.
